questions.text:
A soap bubble, having radius of 1 mm, is blown from a detergent solution having a surface tension of $2.5 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{m}$. The pressure inside the bubble equals at a point $\mathbf{Z}_{0}$ below the free surface of water in a container. Taking $\mathbf{g}=\mathbf{1 0 ~ m} \boldsymbol{/} \mathbf{s}^{\mathbf{2}}$, density of water $=\mathbf{1 0}^{\mathbf{3}} \mathbf{~ k g} / \mathbf{m}^{\mathbf{3}}$, the value of $Z_{0}$ is :
(1) 100 cm
(2) 10 cm
(3) 1 cm
(4) 0.5 cm
Answer (3)

steps:
Excess pressure $=\frac{4 \mathrm{~T}}{\mathrm{R}}$, Gauge pressure
$$\begin{array}{l}
=\rho g Z_{0} \\
P_{0}+\frac{4 T}{R}=P_{0}+\rho g Z_{0} \\
Z_{0}=\frac{4 T}{R \times \rho g} \\
Z_{0}=\frac{4 \times 2.5 \times 10^{-2}}{10^{-3} \times 1000 \times 10} \mathrm{~m} \\
Z_{0}=1 \mathrm{~cm}
\end{array}$$

questions.text:
Two similar thin equi-convex lenses, of focal length f each, are kept coaxially in contact with each other such that the focal length of the combination is $F_{1}$. When the space between the two lenses is filled with glycerine (which has the same refractive index $(\mu=1.5)$ as that of glass) then the equivalent focal length is $F_{2}$. The ratio $F_{1}: F_{2}$ will be :
(1) 2 : 1
(2) 1 : 2
(3) 2 : 3
(4) 3 : 4
Answer (2)
NEET Exam Solution
2
Saral

steps:
Equivalent focal length in air $\frac{1}{\mathrm{~F}_{1}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{f}}=\frac{2}{\mathrm{f}}$
When glycerin is filled inside, glycerin lens behaves like a diverging lens of focal length (-f)
$$\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{F_{2}} & =\frac{1}{f}+\frac{1}{f}-\frac{1}{f} \\
& =\frac{1}{f} \\
\frac{F_{1}}{F_{2}} & =\frac{1}{2}
\end{aligned}$$

questions.text:
Six similar bulbs are connected as shown in the figure with a DC source of emf E and zero internal resistance.
The ratio of power consumption by the bulbs when (i) all are glowing and (ii) in the situation when two from section $A$ and one from section B are glowing, will be :
(1) 4 : 9
(2) $9: 4$
(3) 1 : 2
(4) 2 : 1
Answer (2)

steps:
(i) All bulbs are glowing
$$\begin{array}{l}
R_{\text {eq }}=\frac{R}{3}+\frac{R}{3}=\frac{2 R}{3} \\
\operatorname{Power}\left(P_{i}\right)=\frac{E^{2}}{R_{\text {eq }}}=\frac{3 E^{2}}{2 R}
\end{array}$$
(ii) Two from section A and one from section B are glowing.
$$\begin{array}{l}
R_{e q}=\frac{R}{2}+R=\frac{3 R}{2} \\
\operatorname{Power}\left(P_{f}\right)=\frac{2 E^{2}}{3 R} \quad \ldots(2) \\
\frac{P_{i}}{P_{f}}=\frac{3 E^{2} 3 R}{2 R 2 E^{2}}=9: 4
\end{array}$$

A force $\mathrm{F}=20+10 \mathrm{y}$ acts on a particle in ydirection where F is in newton and y in meter. Work done by this force to move the particle from $\mathrm{y}=0$ to $\mathrm{y}=1 \mathrm{~m}$ is
(1) 30 J
(2) 5 J
(3) 25 J
(4) 20 J
Answer (3)

steps:
Work done by variable force is
$$W=\int_{y_{i}}^{y_{f}} F d y$$

Here, $y_{i}=0, y_{f}=1 \mathrm{~m}$
$$\therefore W=\int_{0}^{1}(20+10 y) d y=\left[20 y+\frac{10 y^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{1}=25 \mathrm{~J}$$

questions.text:
A hollow metal sphere of radius $R$ is uniformly charged. The electric field due to the sphere at a distance r from the centre
(1) Increases as r increase for r < R and for $r>R$
(2) Zero as r increases for r < R, decreases as r increases for r > R
(3) Zero as r increases for r < R, increases as r increases for r > R
(4) Decreases as $r$ increases for $r<R$ and for $r>R$
Answer (2)
NEET Exam Solution
5
Saral

steps:
Charge $Q$ will be distributed over the surface of hollow metal sphere.
(i) For $\mathrm{r}<\mathrm{R}$ (inside)

By Gauss law, $\oint \overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}_{\text {in }} \cdot \overrightarrow{\mathrm{d} \mathbf{S}}=\frac{\mathrm{q}_{\text {en }}}{\varepsilon_{0}}=0$
$$\Rightarrow \mathrm{E}_{\text {in }}=0 \quad\left(\because \mathrm{q}_{\text {en }}=0\right)$$
(ii) For $\mathrm{r}>\mathrm{R}$ (outside)
$$\begin{array}{l}
\oint \vec{E}_{0} \cdot \overrightarrow{d S}=\frac{q_{e n}}{\varepsilon_{0}} \\
\text { Here, } q_{e n}=Q\left(\because q_{e n}=Q\right) \\
\therefore E_{0} 4 \pi r^{2}=\frac{Q}{\varepsilon_{0}} \\
\therefore E_{0} \propto \frac{1}{r^{2}}
\end{array}$$

questions.text:
The work done to raise a mass $m$ from the surface of the earth to a height $h$, which is equal to the radius of the earth, is:
(1) mgR
(2) 2mgR
(3) $\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{mgR}$
(4) $\frac{3}{2} \mathrm{mgR}$
Answer (3)

steps:
Initial potential energy at earths surface is
$$U_{i}=\frac{-G M m}{R}$$

Final potential energy at height $\mathrm{h}=\mathrm{R}$
$$U_{f}=\frac{-G M m}{2 R}$$

As work done = Change in PE
$$\begin{aligned}
\therefore & W=U_{f}-U_{i} \\
& =\frac{G M m}{2 R}=\frac{g R^{2} m}{2 R}=\frac{m g R}{2} \quad\left(\because G M=g R^{2}\right)
\end{aligned}$$

questions.text:
When an object is shot from the bottom of a long smooth inclined plane kept at an angle 60° with horizontal, it can travel a distance $\times 1$ along the plane. But when the inclination is decreased to 30° and the same object is shot with the same velocity, it can travel $\mathrm{x}_{2}$ distance. Then $\mathrm{x}_{1}: \mathrm{x}_{2}$ will be:
(1) $1: \sqrt{2}$
(2) $\sqrt{2}: 1$
(3) $1: \sqrt{3}$
(4) $1: 2 \sqrt{3}$
Answer (3)

steps:
(Stopping distance) $\quad \mathrm{x}_{1}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^{2}}{2 \mathrm{~g} \sin 60^{\circ}}$
(Stopping distance) $\quad \mathrm{x}_{2}=\frac{\mathrm{u}^{2}}{2 \mathrm{~g} \sin 30^{\circ}}$
$$\Rightarrow \frac{x_{1}}{x_{2}}=\frac{\sin 30^{\circ}}{\sin 60^{\circ}}=\frac{1 \times 2}{2 \times \sqrt{3}}=1: \sqrt{3}$$

questions.text:
Two particles A and B are moving in uniform circular motion in concentric circles of radii $r_{A}$ and $r_{B}$ with speed $v_{A}$ and $v_{B}$ respectively. Their time period of rotation is the same. The ratio of angular speed of A to that of B will be :

$$T_{A}=T_{B}=T$$

questions.text:
A block of mass 10 kg is in contact against the inner wall of a hollow cylindrical drum of radius 1 m . The coefficient of friction between the block and the inner wall of the cylinder is 0.1. The minimum angular velocity needed for the cylinder to keep the block stationary when the cylinder is vertical and rotating about its axis, will be : $\left(\mathbf{g}=\mathbf{1 0 ~ m} / \mathbf{s}^{\mathbf{2}}\right)$
(1) $\sqrt{\mathbf{1 0}} \mathbf{~ r a d} \boldsymbol{/} \mathbf{s}$
(2) $\frac{10}{2 \pi} \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$
(3) 10 rad/s
(4) $10 \pi \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$
Answer (3)

steps:
For equilibrium of the block limiting friction
$$\begin{aligned}
& f_{L} \geq m g \\
\Rightarrow & \mu N \geq m g \\
\Rightarrow & \mu m r \omega^{2} \geq m g \\
& \omega \geq \sqrt{\frac{g}{r \mu}} \\
& \omega_{\min }=\sqrt{\frac{g}{r \mu}} \\
& \omega_{\min }=\sqrt{\frac{10}{0.1 \times 1}}=10 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$$

questions.text:
Two parallel infinite line charges with linear charge densities $+\lambda \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}$ and $-\lambda \mathrm{C} / \mathrm{m}$ are placed at a distance of 2R in free space. What is the electric field mid-way between the two line charges?
(1) Zero
(2) $\frac{2 \lambda}{\pi \varepsilon_{0} \mathrm{R}} \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{C}$
(3) $\frac{\lambda}{\pi \varepsilon_{0} \mathrm{R}} \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{C}$
(4) $\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi \varepsilon_{0} R} N / C$
Answer (3)
NEET Exam Solution
8
Saral

steps: $$-x \longleftarrow x$$

Electric field due to line charge (1)
$$\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}_{1}=\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi \varepsilon_{0} \mathrm{R}} \hat{\mathrm{i}} \mathrm{~N} / \mathrm{C}$$

Electric field due to line charge (2)
$$\begin{aligned}
\vec{E}_{2} & =\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi \varepsilon_{0} R} \hat{i} N / C \\
\vec{E}_{\text {net }} & =\vec{E}_{1}+\vec{E}_{2} \\
& =\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi \varepsilon_{0} R} \hat{i}+\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi \varepsilon_{0} R} \hat{i} \\
& =\frac{\lambda}{\pi \varepsilon_{0} R} \hat{i} N / C

questions.text:
A 800 turn coil of effective area $0.05 \mathrm{~m}^{2}$ is kept perpendicular to a magnetic field $5 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~T}$. When the plane of the coil is rotated by 90° around any of its coplanar axis in 0.1 s, the emf induced in the coil will be:
(1) 2 V
(2) 0.2 V
(3) $2 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~V}$
(4) 0.02 V
Answer (4)

steps:
Magnetic field $\mathrm{B}=5 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~T}$
Number of turns in coil $\mathbf{N} \boldsymbol{=} \mathbf{8 0 0}$
Area of coil A $=0.05 \mathrm{~m}^{2}$
Time taken to rotate $\Delta \mathrm{t}=0.1 \mathrm{~s}$
Initial angle $\theta_{1}=0^{\circ}$
Final angle $\theta_{2}=90^{\circ}$
Change in magnetic flux $\Delta \phi$
$$\begin{array}{l}
=\mathrm{NBAcos} 90^{\circ}-\mathrm{BAcos} 0^{\circ} \\
=-\mathrm{NBA} \\
=-800 \times 5 \times 10^{-5} \times 0.05 \\
=-2 \times 10^{-3} \text { weber } \\
\mathrm{e}=-\frac{\Delta \phi}{\Delta \mathrm{t}}=\frac{-(-) 2 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~Wb}}{0.1 \mathrm{~s}}=0.02 \mathrm{~V}
\end{array}$$

questions.text:
A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance $20 \mu \mathrm{~F}$ is being charged by a voltage source whose potential is changing at the rate of $3 \mathrm{~V} / \mathrm{s}$. The conduction current through the connecting wires, and the displacement current through the plates of the capacitor, would be, respectively.
(1) Zero, $60 \mu \mathrm{~A}$
(2) $60 \mu \mathrm{~A}, 60 \mu \mathrm{~A}$
(3) $\mathbf{6 0} \mu \mathbf{A}$, zero
(4) Zero, zero
Answer (2)

steps:
Capacitance of capacitor $\mathbf{C}=\mathbf{2 0} \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{F}$
$$=20 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~F}$$

Rate of change of potential $\left(\frac{\mathbf{d V}}{\mathbf{d t}}\right)=\mathbf{3 ~ v} / \mathbf{s}$
$$\begin{aligned}
q & =C V \\
\frac{d q}{d t} & =C \frac{d V}{d t} \\
i_{c} & =20 \times 10^{-6} \times 3 \\
& =60 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{~A} \\
& =60 \mu \mathrm{~A}
\end{aligned}$$
As we know that $i_{d}=i_{c}=60 \mu \mathrm{~A}$

questions.text:
In an experiment, the percentage of error occurred in the measurement of physical quantities A, B, C and D are 1\%, 2\%, 3\% and 4\% respectively. Then the maximum percentage of error in the measurement $X$, where $X=\frac{A^{2} B^{1 / 2}}{C^{1 / 3} D^{3}}$, will be
(1) $\left(\frac{\mathbf{3}}{\mathbf{1 3}}\right) \%$
(2) 16\%
(3) - 10\%
(4) 10\%
Answer (2)

steps:
Given
$$\begin{array}{l}
x=\frac{A^{2} B^{\frac{1}{2}}}{C^{\frac{1}{3}} D^{3}} \\
\% \text { error, } \frac{\Delta x}{x} \times 100=2 \frac{\Delta A}{A} \times 100+\frac{1}{2} \frac{\Delta B}{B} \times \\
100+\frac{1}{3} \frac{\Delta C}{C} \times 100+3 \frac{\Delta D}{D} \times 100
\end{array}$$
$$\begin{array}{l}
=2 \times 1 \%+\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \%+\frac{1}{3} \times 3 \%+3 \times 4 \% \\
=2 \%+1 \%+1 \%+12 \% \\
=16 \%
\end{array}$$
